title: iterate-review reviewer output
description: Structured output from Codex reviewing a code diff via the iterate-review skill. Enforced by codex exec --output-schema. All four top-level array fields are required-but-may-be-empty.

verdict.description: APPROVE = code is structurally sound, ready to ship; REVISE = at least one load-bearing issue to fix; BLOCK = fundamental problem that invalidates the change's premise (rare).

findings.description: Substantive issues with the code change. Required field; may be empty if verdict=APPROVE with nothing to flag.

severity.description: HIGH = load-bearing, would cause incorrect behavior or break invariants if shipped; always blocks APPROVE. MEDIUM = real issue worth addressing; doesn't block APPROVE if the editor disputes/explains, but considered. LOW = nit, polish, stylistic.

description.description: Full text of the issue. Cite file paths and line numbers from the diff when useful (e.g., 'web/lib/foo.ts:42 introduces an unguarded null deref'). Be concrete.

suggested_action.description: What the editor should consider doing about it. May be open-ended ('clarify the contract') or specific ('add a null check before line 42'). Describe intent, not the literal patch text.

register_ref.description: REQUIRED FIELD, but set it to null in the common case. Set to a register id ONLY when this finding is independently actionable AND its behavior falls within a specific entry's recorded bound/recovery in the accepted-risks register (docs/risk-posture.md, provided in the RISK POSTURE block when present). Do not set this to merely reference a posture decision — if a finding only restates something the register or posture already covers with no new evidence, don't file it at all. Do not set this if you are presenting evidence that the entry's bound or recovery path is false — that is a fresh finding, not a match, even if it concerns the same behavior. The editor validates every non-null register_ref against the current register at fold time; an unknown, malformed, or non-matching ref is treated as untagged.

code_corrections.description: Tactical non-controversial fixes (typos in comments, broken imports, dead code, contradictions between docstring and behavior). Required; may be empty. Distinct from findings in that corrections are mechanical and the editor should incorporate them without dispute.

location.description: File path with line number when known (e.g., 'web/app/page.tsx:120', 'pipeline/foo.py:fn_name'). For changes spanning multiple lines, use a range or the function/section name.

fix.description: What it should be, in abstract terms. The editor does the actual edit.

new_questions.description: Questions you want answered in the next pass — typically clarifications about author intent or constraints not visible in the diff — each classified by WHO CAN SETTLE IT. Required; may be empty. If you can answer a question yourself from the diff and intent you were given, say so in a finding instead of filing it here.

settled_by.description: Who can settle this. 'resolvable_in_fold' = answerable from the repository the diff came from — you see only the diff, so the editor can read the surrounding code, callers, and tests you cannot. 'needs_lookup' = a fact exists that settles it, but reaching that fact requires something you cannot do (a network call, an API query, running the test suite or a benchmark). 'needs_human' = no fact and no derivation settles it; it needs the author's intent, risk tolerance, cost appetite, or product judgment. WHEN UNSURE, CHOOSE 'needs_human' — wrongly labelling an author's decision as machine-resolvable invites a fabricated answer, which is far worse than an unnecessary escalation.

why.description: One line justifying the classification — e.g. which file you'd need to read, what lookup would settle it, or which judgment only the author can make. This exists so the label can be audited rather than trusted; a bare enum is easy to rubber-stamp.
